chunks: His father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan - may God be pleased with them - said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadl, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the words of the Exalted: 'Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every liar, sinful one.' He said: They are seven: Al-Mughira, Binan, Sa'id, Hamza ibn 'Amara al-Barbari, al-Harith al-Shami, Abdullah ibn al-Harith, and Abu al-Khattab.

key_terms.أَثِيمٍ: Sinful, one who bears the burden of sin
key_terms.أَفَّاكٍ: A liar, one who tells falsehoods

ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people upon whom the devils descend according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifying seven specific historical figures—ranging from early Islamic opponents like Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah to later boasters—as the archetypes upon whom devils descend, linking their personal traits of falsehood to the Quranic description in Surah Al-Muddaththir. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of interpreting Quranic verses through specific historical exemplars (tafsir bi-l-ma'thur), providing a concrete application of spiritual corruption to known personalities.
